topics.label: Introduction and Course Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students, introduces the scope of the cancer biology lecture series, and outlines the primary learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cancer as a Failure of Genetic Regulation and Tissue Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as a multistep disruption of genetic programming and developmental tissue organization while addressing the methods and challenges of modeling these cellular changes in culture.

topics.label: Tumor Invasion, Metastasis, and Stepwise Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biological processes and histological hallmarks of local tissue invasion and distant metastasis, using the colorectal adenoma-to-carcinoma sequence as a primary example.

topics.label: Benign Tumor Behavior and Tumor Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the clinical significance and physical risks associated with benign neoplasms alongside the standardized naming conventions used to classify benign and malignant tumors.

topics.label: Pathophysiology of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the physiological mechanisms, mechanical obstructions, and systemic failures through which primary tumors and distant metastases cause patient illness and death.

topics.label: Tumor Incidence and Comparative Oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze patterns of cancer incidence and tissue susceptibility across human populations and diverse animal species to highlight cancer as a universal disease of multicellular differentiation.

topics.label: Principles and Clinical Applications of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical rationale for early cancer detection and compare the diagnostic approaches, effectiveness, and limitations of screening programs across different anatomical sites.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Practical Preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session by reiterating the core learning outcomes and previewing the upcoming practical coursework.
